texts: Caffeine doesn't actually give you energy—it just blocks your brain's "tired" signals, so adenosine (the sleep chemical) builds up completely unnoticed while you feel alert, meaning coffee drinkers are constantly running a sleep deficit they can't feel.

The coffee berry borer beetle spends its entire life inside coffee cherries, making it the only beetle known to spend almost its entire life underground inside a fruit—infesting up to 50% of a farm's harvest and causing over $500 million in annual global damages.

During the 1989 fall of the Berlin Wall, East Germans traded raw coffee beans on the black market at prices equivalent to a month's salary for a simple cup, making coffee the unofficial currency of escape and one of the most valued commodities behind the Iron Curtain.
